title: Topological Quantum Spin Liquids in a Ladder with Majorana fermions and p-wave Superconductivity
authors: Magali Korolev, Fan Yang, Erik S. Sørensen, Karyn Le Hur
abstract: In this article, we address the possibility of topological quantum spin liquids with only short-range (spin) correlations in the whole phase diagram in a ladder system, through an exactly solvable model which represents a generalization of the two-dimensional Kitaev honeycomb spin model to a ribbon geometry. This system gives rise to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge fields emerging in a static way in the ground state through Majorana fermions which then produce either $0$ or $π$ flux. Through a quantum field theory perspective, mathematical and Density Matrix Renormalization Group results, we present our progress on the geometrical, topological and physical classification of this model through observables navigating on the whole phase diagram presenting three spin-liquid phases with a spin gap and a metallic phase in the sense of Majorana fermions. We propose a bulk-edge correspondence revealing the presence of protected zero-energy Majorana fermions at the edge in the phases with a gap and revealing also the presence of itinerant Majorana fermions in the bulk in the topological liquid phase. The proposed approach allows us to distinguish between properties of the brickwall ladder giving rise to a special line and those of the square ladder allowing for the gapless Majorana liquid phase. This model gives some hope on finding solutions for topological quantum spin models, e.g. with $π$ flux, on a square lattice geometry. This approach also allows for a correspondence onto models of topological superconductivity.
summary: This work analyzes a generalized ladder spin model to explore topological quantum spin liquid phases. By mapping the system onto Majorana fermions and applying advanced theoretical tools, the authors classify the phase diagram, predicting protected Majorana edge modes in gapped phases. This establishes a strong theoretical link between frustrated magnetism and topological superconductivity.
main_problem: The paper investigates the existence and properties of topological quantum spin liquids in a ladder system, specifically linking magnetic models to $p$-wave superconductivity.
main_result: The model predicts three distinct spin-liquid phases and a metallic phase, characterized by a bulk-edge correspondence that reveals protected zero-energy Majorana fermions at the edges in gapped regions.
method: The analysis employs a combination of quantum field theory, Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) techniques, and mathematical diagonalization of the Majorana fermion representation.
model_or_system: The system is a generalized ladder geometry, modeled as a spin Hamiltonian derived from a generalization of the Kitaev honeycomb model. It is mapped onto Majorana fermions coupled via $Z_2$ gauge fields.

Topological invariant ($

important_parameters: Coupling constants ($J_1, J_2, J_3, J_4$) and the relative signs of these couplings, which determine the flux sector ($	ext{0}$ or $\pi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis initially focuses on the case where all couplings $J_i \ge 0$, though the method is shown to be generalizable.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ladder structure with couplings and Majorana fermions, the phase diagram showing three spin-liquid phases and a metallic phase, and diagrams detailing the flux selection based on coupling signs.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the Hamiltonian, mapping it to Majorana fermions, utilizing quantum field theory and DMRG to classify the topological phases via observables, and finally establishing the bulk-edge correspondence.
why_interesting: The rigorous connection established between magnetic spin models (quantum spin liquids) and topological superconductivity via Majorana fermions is highly relevant for understanding emergent phenomena in condensed matter systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Illustration of the ladder. The color blue refers to the coupling J1, the color green to the coupling J2, the color yellow to the coupling J3 and the color orange to the coupling J4. We also illustrate the presence at each site of the Majorana fermions cj and dj. The Majorana fermions dj encode the presence of a macroscopic degeneracy associated to the ground state e.g. for a blue link we have the two possible ground states | +x −x⟩and | −x +x⟩. The Majorana fermions dj in the ladder geometry then encode the Z2 gauge fields that result in the loop operator Wp = ±1 referring to 0, π flux ground state.

Figure 2. Phase diagram for generic Ji’s including three quantum spin liquid phases Ax, Ay, Az, with a gap in the bulk, and the Majorana liquid phase B. The metallic phase B refers to the surface with ||J1| −|J2|| = p

Figure 3. Generalized Lieb theorem on the ladder geometry. In the ground state, the flux sector (red arrow) selects (a) Wp = −1, π flux when the number of AFM couplings (Ji > 0) is even and (b) Wp = +1, 0 flux when odd. The (±) signs are assigned to the linking variables uν j,k = ibν j bν k following the direction of black arrows on the bonds.
